summary: The investigation did not identify a definitive root cause for the pricing-engine latency degradation. Evidence shows a CPU spike in market-data-service preceding the latency onset and increased error rates, while pricing-engine resources remained stable. However, missing deployment, configuration, and latency metrics for downstream services prevent a conclusive attribution.

facts.statement: No deployments were recorded for pricing-engine between 2026-04-09T00:00:00Z and 2026-04-09T14:59:00Z.
No configuration changes were recorded for pricing-engine in the same period.
The overall deployments list is incomplete; only one deployment (auth-service v7.2.0 at 2026-04-09T11:30:00Z) was returned with a warning of missing shards.
Pricing-engine depends on market-data-service (http) and redis-cache (cache); it is also called by order-service (http) and indirectly by api-gateway via order-service.
Redis-cache is a shared datastore used by multiple services (pricing-engine, market-data-service, etc.).
Pricing-engine p99 latency spikes above 2000 ms at 2026-04-09T13:22:00Z, marking the onset of the degradation.
Pricing-engine p99 latency remains elevated (avg > 2200 ms) through 13:24‑13:30 Z.
Pricing-engine logs contain repeated deadline‑exceeded errors: "quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <n>ms".
Market-data-service error_rate jumps from ~0.2 % to >1 % at 13:18 Z and stays around 3 % thereafter.
No other services in the queried set show elevated p99 latency; the only latency spike observed is in pricing-engine.
Pricing-engine CPU usage stayed roughly constant (≈39‑41 %) from 13:00 to 14:56 Z, with no spike at the latency onset.
Pricing-engine memory usage remained stable around 48‑51 % throughout the window, with no notable increase at 13:22 Z.
Market-data-service CPU usage spiked sharply starting at 13:20 Z, reaching an average of ~90 % and a max of ~94 % by 13:24 Z, and stayed elevated thereafter.
Redis-cache CPU usage stayed flat around 21‑22 % for the entire period, showing no spike concurrent with the pricing-engine latency degradation.

assumptions: No deployments or configuration changes occurred for market-data-service, redis-cache, order-service, or other downstream components during the incident window (due to missing records).
The latency spikes observed in pricing-engine are caused by downstream request latency rather than internal processing bottlenecks, based on stable CPU/memory on pricing-engine.

recommended_actions.action: Throttle or temporarily reduce request rate from pricing-engine to market-data-service (e.g., enable rate limiting or circuit breaker).
recommended_actions.rationale: Market-data-service CPU is saturated (~90 %); reducing load may relieve pressure and restore latency.

recommended_actions.action: Restart market-data-service to clear any transient resource contention.
recommended_actions.rationale: A quick restart can free CPU and may immediately reduce deadline‑exceeded errors while longer diagnostics run.

recommended_actions.action: Collect missing deployment and configuration change records for market-data-service, redis-cache, and order-service (e.g., query CI/CD logs, config management DB).
recommended_actions.rationale: Current gaps prevent confirming whether a recent change caused the CPU spike.

recommended_actions.action: Retrieve and store market-data-service latency_p99_ms metric (resolve backend 503) and pricing-db resource metrics (CPU, memory, connection pool latency).
recommended_actions.rationale: Direct latency evidence and DB load data are needed to validate the downstream pressure hypothesis.

recommended_actions.action: Implement continuous health checks and alerts for downstream services (CPU >80 %, error_rate >1 %) that feed into pricing-engine SLA monitoring.
recommended_actions.rationale: Proactive detection of downstream resource saturation will prevent similar latency degradations.

recommended_actions.action: Improve deployment inventory completeness (ensure all shards are captured) and integrate with incident response tooling.
recommended_actions.rationale: Incomplete deployment data (F3) hampers root‑cause analysis in future incidents.
